html:
The Suez Crisis was the invasion of Egypt by Israel, Britain and France in late 1956, after Egypt took over the Suez Canal, and their forced withdrawal under American and Soviet pressure.

In July 1956 the United States and Britain withdrew their offer to help pay for the Aswan High Dam. Gamal Abdel Nasser answered by nationalising the Suez Canal Company, still owned mostly by British and French shareholders, to use its tolls for the dam. Britain saw the canal, open since 1869, as its lifeline to the east, and France was angry at Nasser's help to the rebels in Algeria.

The three countries made a secret plan. On 29 October Israel invaded the Sinai. Britain and France then ordered both sides to pull back from the canal and, when Egypt refused, bombed Egyptian airfields and landed at Port Said in early November. Egypt sank ships to block the canal.

The United States, angry at not being told, put heavy pressure on the British pound, and the Soviet Union made threats. A ceasefire came on 7 November, and the first United Nations peacekeeping force took over. Britain and France left by December, Israel by March 1957.

Nasser became a hero across the Arab world, and the crisis showed that Britain was no longer a great power that could act alone. Egypt then expelled many British, French and Jewish residents (Jewish exodus from Arab lands). Egypt, Iraq and Lebanon boycotted the Melbourne Olympics in protest.
sum: The Suez Crisis was the invasion of Egypt by Israel, Britain and France in late 1956, after Egypt took over the Suez Canal, and their forced withdrawal under American and Soviet pressure.
